signal: Onspring launched new AI capabilities for its GRC platform in June 2026

email.body1:
Rene, saw Onspring just launched AI capabilities across the GRC platform.

A launch like that lights up more enterprise accounts than the team can work before interest cools, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount, 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Onspring off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing those tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Rene, quick follow-up for Onspring.

Right after a major launch, expectations on pipeline usually jump faster than enterprise headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Onspring needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Rene, last bit of proof for Onspring.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Onspring's reply rate likely compares to other GRC software vendors. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Rene, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling enterprise pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. A launch cycle is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an enterprise GRC motion? I'll tailor it to Onspring either way.
